step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Analyzed the visual entities from the diagram: Scheduled Lambda functions at the top center, KMS at top right, S3 bucket and EC2 instances in the Static Analysis column, DynamoDB at bottom left for state and results storage, AWS Batch in the Open Source column scanning external Internet sources (GitHub, GitLab, Jira) and invoking deep learning Docker containers.
2. Identified the flows described in the video:
   - Flow 0 (Static Analysis): Scheduled Lambda functions trigger/spin up EC2 instances. EC2 handles binary processing and stores binaries in S3 encrypted with KMS keys. EC2 writes scan state and analysis results to DynamoDB.
   - Flow 1 (Open Source Scanning): AWS Batch scours public Internet repositories continuously and feeds data into Docker containers running machine learning models to assess vulnerability true positives.
3. Normalized node services against the allowed vocabulary list, mapping external tools (Docker, Internet) to ThirdParty.
4. Formatted output into valid JSON following all strict rules without control tokens.

graph.name: Veracode Static Analysis and Open Source Vulnerability Scanning Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture powering Veracode static code analysis and open source vulnerability detection using AWS compute and machine learning.

nodes.name: Scheduled Lambda Functions
nodes.notes: Scheduled Lambda functions that trigger and spin up EC2 instances to process incoming application binaries at scale.

nodes.name: AWS KMS
nodes.notes: Provides customer-unique encryption keys to secure application binaries stored at rest in S3.

nodes.name: S3 Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores customer application binaries securely at rest with KMS key encryption.

nodes.name: EC2 Analysis Instances
nodes.notes: Spun up in dynamic compute sizes to perform static analysis and build software vulnerability graphs within seconds or minutes.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores analysis state, process metadata, and historical result data (over 10.5 trillion lines of code scanned).

nodes.name: AWS Batch
nodes.notes: Scours public internet repositories continuously 24/7 to pull commit and defect ticket data for open source vulnerability assessment.

nodes.name: Docker Containers
nodes.notes: Executes deep learning machine learning containers/pipelines to evaluate true positive vulnerabilities in open source components.

nodes.name: Internet Sources
nodes.notes: External repositories and issue tracking platforms including GitHub, GitLab, and Jira.

edges.notes: Scheduled Lambda function spins up EC2 instances based on incoming analysis workload.
EC2 instance stores received binaries into the S3 bucket for analysis.
S3 leverages AWS KMS customer-specific keys to encrypt binaries at rest.
EC2 writes state information and scan results into DynamoDB.
AWS Batch pulls commit and issue data from public internet sources.
AWS Batch triggers deep learning ML pipelines running in Docker containers.
